recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Do not restore Supply, SupplyRequest, or SupplyDelivery to FHIR core for FHIR-6067; make future definition-level changes in HL7/oo-incubator and update core only if its incubator links become stale.
issue_request: FHIR-6067 is a Published FHIR-core change request resolved Persuasive with Modification. It asked to split the original Supply resource; the final resolution says Supply was split into SupplyRequest and SupplyDelivery, both remaining Draft resources, with follow-up trackers for adjacent scope questions.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in git history by 1594fb6cad29ec60b476d6167a1f7bf6a810291b, titled '#6067Split Supply into SupplyRequest and SupplyDelivery', which added SupplyRequest and SupplyDelivery entries to source/fhir.ini and related metadata. The Jira resolution also states the split was pre-applied.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini has no active [resources] entries for SupplyRequest or SupplyDelivery, while [removed-resources] lists the old Supply resource. Later commit 3b38b80cf23f9cbb306fab8fcedb293315478c32 removed OO resources from core and retargeted core narrative links to the HL7 OO Incubator continuous build. Current core pages link SupplyRequest and SupplyDelivery to build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/oo-incubator, whose pages identify github.com/HL7/oo-incubator as the current source.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No core source was changed because reintroducing or editing SupplyRequest/SupplyDelivery definitions would be out of current core build scope.

related_jiras.note: Follow-up from the seed discussion about whether DeviceUseRequest should roll into SupplyRequest; inspected as context but not decided because it is a separate DeviceUseRequest boundary decision.

Follow-up from the seed discussion about whether VisionPrescription should become a SupplyRequest or DeviceUseRequest profile; inspected as context but not decided because it is a separate VisionPrescription decision.
The seed comment names tracker 7632 for bulk supply, but the indexed FHIR-7632 snapshot is an unrelated Procedure.used no-change issue, so it was not treated as a supply-split decision.
